ledger.x: 1260: the Empire in the Interregnum, as Cliopatria's second row begins.
1268: the Hohenstaufen duchy of Swabia falls to the king's direct rule.
1272: Carinthia and the Slovene lands pass to Bohemia's Cliopatria shape.
1272: Umbria and the Marche pass to the Papal States' Cliopatria shape.
1272: 34 cells of Bavaria pass to Cliopatria's Duchy of Bavaria shape.
1272: 17 cells of Pomerania pass to the Margraviate of Brandenburg's Cliopatria shape.
1272: Tyrol and South Tyrol come into this row from the shape Cliopatria calls the Duchy of Styria.
1273: Rudolf of Habsburg is elected king after Richard of Cornwall's death; same state, new dynasty.
1279: Romagna and the Pentapolis pass to the Papal States' Cliopatria shape.
1294: 106 cells (Carinthia 35, Baden-Wurttemberg 9, Lucerne 7, Aargau 4) return from the House of Habsburg's Cliopatria shape.
1294: 27 cells of Luxembourg and Liege return from the House of Luxembourg's Cliopatria shape.
ledger.cpn: County and Duchy of Luxembourg (House of Luxembourg)

ledger.x: 1294: 25 cells (Rhineland-Palatinate 21) return from Cliopatria's Duchy of Bavaria shape.
1308: Henry VII of Luxembourg is elected after Albert I's assassination; same state, new dynasty.
1314: Louis IV of Wittelsbach becomes king (emperor 1328-1347); same state, new dynasty, per the page (king from 1314, emperor 1328-1347).
1326: 15 cells of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern come in from the Kingdom of Denmark's Cliopatria shape.
1333: Franche-Comte is cut out for the Free County of Burgundy's own Cliopatria shape; it stays a member of the Empire's umbrella.
1333: 26 cells (Lower Silesia 16, Saxony 6) pass to Bohemia's Cliopatria shape.
1344: 77 cells (Carinthia 35, Styria, Carniola) pass to the House of Habsburg's Cliopatria shape.
1344: 17 cells of Brandenburg pass to Bohemia's Cliopatria shape.
1352: Tyrol and South Tyrol pass to Cliopatria's Duchy of Bavaria shape.
1355: Charles IV's court makes Prague the seat of the emperor.
1363: 21 cells (Saxony-Anhalt 10, Brandenburg 8, Saxony 3) pass to the Electorate of Saxony's Cliopatria shape, which begins this year.
1375: Mecklenburg is drawn inside Cliopatria's Kingdom of Sweden shape until 1394.
1395: Mecklenburg leaves the Kingdom of Sweden's Cliopatria shape and returns to this row.
1395: the Swiss Confederation's Cliopatria shape is cut out of it.
1395: 26 cells of Piedmont (Turin 13, Cuneo 5, Biella 4, Vercelli 2) pass to the County of Savoy's Cliopatria shape.
1402: Lombardy passes to the Duchy of Milan's Cliopatria shape, which begins this year.
1402: 42 cells (Ain 11, Vaud 11, Haute-Savoie 9, Isere 4) pass to the County of Savoy's Cliopatria shape.
1407: the Veneto passes to the Republic of Venice's Cliopatria shape.
1415: 52 cells of Luxembourg and Liege (Luxembourg 20, Liege 8, Rhineland-Palatinate 4, Diekirch 4) pass to the County of Brabant's Cliopatria shape; they return to this row in 1422.
1422: the 52 Luxembourg and Liege cells return from the County of Brabant's Cliopatria shape.

1422: the Electorate of Brandenburg's first Cliopatria shape takes 21 cells of Bavaria (Franconia) from this row; the other 156 cells it covers are the Mark, already outside this row after the 1415 correction.
1429: 44 cells of Luxembourg (Luxembourg 20, Liege 4, Diekirch 4, Luxembourg 4) pass to Cliopatria's Duchy of Luxembourg shape.
1431: Lorraine and Bar pass to the Duchy of Lorraine's Cliopatria shape, which begins this year; the Duchy of Lorraine dossier dates the duchy's start to January 1431 from its own page.
1440: the 18 Franconian cells (Bavaria) that Cliopatria's Electorate of Brandenburg shape held since 1422 return to this row.
1459: Holstein passes to the Kalmar Union's Cliopatria shape.
1459: 11 cells (St.
1475: 26 cells of the Low Countries (Flevoland 7, Gelderland 4, Utrecht 4, Limburg 3) pass to the Duchy of Burgundy's Cliopatria shape.
1481-82: Fribourg and Solothurn join the Swiss.
1492: 22 cells of the Low Countries (Flevoland 7, Gelderland 4, Utrecht 4, Limburg 3) come back from the Habsburg Monarchy's Cliopatria shape.
1497-1501: Graubunden and the border cities attach to the Swiss.
1512: the Diet of Cologne renames the realm 'Holy Roman Empire of the German Nation'; same state, same colour.
1524: Friesland pass to the Habsburg Netherlands.
1528: Utrecht and Overijssel pass to the Habsburg Netherlands.
1529: 12 cells (Valais 10) pass to the Swiss Confederation's Cliopatria shape; the page has the Valais as an associate from 1416 and no 1529 date.
1536: Groningen and Drenthe pass to the Habsburg Netherlands.
1540: 24 cells of Piedmont (Cuneo 14, Turin 7) pass to the Kingdom of France's Cliopatria shape.
1543: Guelders pass to the Habsburg Netherlands.
1552: Henry II of France seizes Metz, Toul and Verdun.
1552: Charles V besieges Metz.
1553: the siege of Metz ends on 2 January and the expedition fails; the French keep the three bishoprics until the Peace of Westphalia cedes them in 1648.
1556: Siena and Grosseto pass to the Republic of Florence's Cliopatria shape.
1556: Thuringia comes into this row from the Electorate of Saxony's Cliopatria shape.
1576: Rudolf II succeeds and holds court at Prague.
1609: 15 cells (Overijssel 6, Zeeland 4, Lower Saxony 3) come in from the Dutch Republic's Cliopatria shape.
1619: 20 cells of the lower Rhine (North Rhine-Westphalia 15) pass to Brandenburg-Prussia's Cliopatria shape.
1626: Christian IV and the Imperial armies fight over the Lower Saxon Circle.
June 1629: the Treaty of Lubeck ends the Danish phase.
1632: the Swedes hold southern Germany.
1635: the Swedish hold ends.
1636: 30 cells of Mecklenburg and Pomerania (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern 21, West Pomerania 6) pass to the Swedish Empire's Cliopatria shape.
1640: Alsace passes to the Kingdom of France's Cliopatria shape.
1642: Mecklenburg is drawn Swedish.
1642: 21 cells (Ardennes 11, Saarland 5, Rhineland-Palatinate 4) pass to the Kingdom of France's Cliopatria shape.
1645: Bremen-Verden passes to the Swedish Empire's Cliopatria shape; Westphalia gives Sweden 'the Prince-Bishoprics of Bremen and Verden as hereditary fiefs' in 1648.
1645: French armies hold Swabian ground.
1648: the Peace of Westphalia gives Brandenburg its Pomeranian and Westphalian lands.
24 October 1648: Cliopatria's 1648 shape has Mecklenburg back in this row (the treaties were signed on 24 October 1648).
24 October 1648: Cliopatria returns the 18 Swabian cells to this row.
1648: Strasbourg stays imperial.
1648: the Lower Palatinate is restored.
1662: 35 cells (Schleswig-Holstein 18, Southern Denmark 16) come in from Denmark-Norway's Cliopatria shape.
1663: the Perpetual Diet sits at Regensburg.
1670: 15 cells of Lower Saxony pass to Denmark-Norway's Cliopatria shape.
1673: Trent and Bolzano pass to the Habsburg Monarchy's Cliopatria shape.
1673: 28 cells of Limburg, Liege and Namur pass to the Kingdom of France's Cliopatria shape.
30 September 1681: France takes Strasbourg.
1683: Magdeburg passes to Brandenburg-Prussia's Cliopatria shape.

1683: 19 cells of Limburg and Liege come back from the Kingdom of France's Cliopatria shape; the 6 cells of Strasbourg and its lands (Bas-Rhin 5) that Cliopatria draws in the France shape from 1683 left this row in 1681 (see the 1681 event).
1696: the Palatinate and Saar pass to the Kingdom of France's Cliopatria shape; the Ryswick page does not mention the Reunions.
1697: the Peace of Ryswick returns the French gains.
1702: 29 cells of Liege, Limburg and Namur pass to the Kingdom of France's Cliopatria shape.
1702: a strip of 5 cells west of the Lech passes to Cliopatria's Duchy of Bavaria shape.
1706: the strip of 5 cells west of the Lech returns from Cliopatria's Duchy of Bavaria shape.
1709: Hanover passes to the Electorate of Hanover's Cliopatria shape.
1713: 32 cells (Southern Denmark 16, Schleswig-Holstein 14) pass to Denmark-Norway's Cliopatria shape.
1713: 25 cells of Liege, Limburg and Namur come in from the Habsburg Monarchy's Cliopatria shape.
1719: on 23 January 1719 'Charles VI, Holy Roman Emperor, decreed that Vaduz and Schellenberg' were united as the Principality of Liechtenstein, the lands having been bought in 1699 and 1712.
1734: Parma and Piacenza pass to the Kingdom of Spain's Cliopatria shape.
1741: Modena, Reggio and Parma pass to the Habsburg Monarchy's Cliopatria shape; they return in 1748.
1741: 18 cells of Swabia and Bavaria pass to the Kingdom of France's Cliopatria shape; they return in 1744.
1744: the 18 cells of Swabia and Bavaria return from the Kingdom of France's Cliopatria shape.
1748: 27 cells (Modena, Reggio Emilia, Parma, Mantua) return from the Habsburg Monarchy's Cliopatria shape.

1757: Hesse and Westphalia pass to the Electorate of Hanover's Cliopatria shape, the year of 'a French Invasion of Hanover' (Hastenbeck, Convention of Klosterzeven); the page names no Hanoverian gain of these cells.
1757: French troops hold Hesse, Westphalia and the Rhineland through the Seven Years' War.
1762: 31 cells (Lower Saxony 20, Thuringia 7) pass to the Electorate of Hanover's Cliopatria shape.
February 1763: the French are out of Germany.
1763: 39 cells (Lower Saxony 25, Thuringia 7) return from the Electorate of Hanover's Cliopatria shape.
1775: 15 cells of Lower Saxony return from Denmark-Norway's Cliopatria shape.
30 December 1777: the Palatinate, Julich and Berg pass to Bavaria.
1791: Franconia passes to the Kingdom of Prussia's Cliopatria shape.
1794: France takes the Rhineland.
1796: Jourdan and Moreau cross the Rhine into Swabia and Franconia.
1796: the French armies are thrown back.
1797: Modena, Reggio, Parma and Mantua pass to the Cisalpine Republic's Cliopatria shape.
1803: the Final Recess of 25 February gives Bavaria the Franconian bishoprics.
1803: Wurttemberg gains Ellwangen, Schontal, Zwiefalten and the cities Heilbronn, Reutlingen and Esslingen, per the page.
1803: Baden gains Constance, the right-bank Speyer and Strasbourg lands and Salem; it 'received over seven times as much' as it lost.
1803: Hesse takes the Duchy of Westphalia and Friedberg.
1803: the 'Grand Duke of Salzburg' receives Eichstatt, Salzburg and Berchtesgaden.
1803: Prussia gains Hildesheim, Munster, Paderborn, Essen, Herford and Quedlinburg; it gained 'nearly five times' what it lost.
1805: 34 cells (Baden-Wurttemberg 12, Bavaria 10, Hesse 10) pass to the First French Empire's Cliopatria shape.
1806: the Confederation of the Rhine takes Berg.
1806: Nassau, a founding member of 12 July 1806.
1806: Hesse-Darmstadt, a founding member of 12 July 1806, becomes a grand duchy.
1806: Wurttemberg, a founding member of 12 July 1806 and a kingdom since Pressburg.
1806: Baden, a founding member of 12 July 1806.
1806: Francis II ends the Holy Roman Empire.
1806: Mecklenburg is outside the Empire when it ends on 6 August 1806; the page does not name Mecklenburg, whose own Cliopatria shape starts this year (Confederation member only from 1808).
1806: Oldenburg is outside the Empire when it ends on 6 August 1806; the page does not name Oldenburg.
1806: 18 cells (Lower Saxony 14) pass to the Kingdom of Prussia's Cliopatria shape.

wars.name: Swabian War
wars.outcome: After the Swabian War of 1499 the Swiss Confederacy was a de facto independent state; Basel and Schaffhausen joined in 1501 and the Three Leagues became associates (1497/98).

wars.name: Siege of Metz
wars.outcome: Charles V besieged Metz from 19 October 1552 to 2 January 1553; the expedition failed and France kept Metz, Toul and Verdun, which the Peace of Westphalia ceded in 1648.

wars.name: Thirty Years' War
wars.outcome: The Peace of Westphalia (24 October 1648): France received the Decapole in Alsace (not Strasbourg), the Three Bishoprics were confirmed, Sweden received Western Pomerania, Wismar, Bremen and Verden, Brandenburg-Prussia Farther Pomerania and the bishoprics of…

wars.name: Thirty Years' War, Danish phase
wars.outcome: Treaty of Lubeck, June 1629: Christian IV kept Schleswig and Holstein, gave up Bremen and Verden and abandoned support for German Protestants.

wars.name: Thirty Years' War, Swedish phase
wars.outcome: Gustavus Adolphus landed in Pomerania in June 1630; Breitenfeld (September 1631) and Rain (April 1632) opened the south; the Imperial-Spanish army won at Nordlingen on 6 September 1634 and the Peace of Prague followed in May 1635.

wars.name: Seven Years' War
wars.outcome: France invaded Hanover in 1757 (Hastenbeck, Convention of Klosterzeven), was driven from Hanover and Westphalia in 1758, took Marburg in 1760, lost Cassel in 1762 and evacuated Prussia's Rhineland territories; the war ended on 10 February 1763 (Treaty of…

wars.name: War of the First Coalition
wars.outcome: After Fleurus (1794) the Rhineland came under French control; Prussia recognised the French occupation of the left bank at Basel (5 April 1795); Jourdan and Moreau were forced back across the Rhine in 1796; Campo Formio (17 October 1797) recognised French…

wars.name: War of the Second Coalition
wars.outcome: After Marengo (14 June 1800) and Hohenlinden (3 December 1800) the Treaty of Luneville (9 February 1801) ceded the entire left bank of the Rhine to France, signed by Francis II for the Empire as well as Austria; princes dispossessed on the left bank were to…

certainty.note: A patchwork of imperial estates, cities and bishoprics whose frontiers are approximate; the Swiss frontier is soft until 1499 and the Dutch frontier from 1581 (the Empire 'de facto' allowed the Netherlands to depart).

The external frontiers 'did not change noticeably' from Westphalia to the dissolution, apart from the loss of Franche-Comte in 1678 (HRE page): the lines fixed by Westphalia (1648), Ryswick (1697) and Luneville (1801) are treaty lines.
